title: Emrys and the Signal
premise: Ada Dunmore, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Kestrel's Rest, has spent twenty years hauling cargo through contested orbits, keeping his head down and his past buried. When a ship that never flew docks with a manifest bearing a name he hasn't heard since the Meridian Massacre—his own brother's—he discovers the station's AI has been quietly preserving erased records of the atrocity. As the fleet's fragile truce expires and both factions hunt the evidence, Ada must decide whether exposing the truth is worth surrendering the identity that kept him alive. In the end, he broadcasts the massacre records fleet-wide at the cost of the station and his anonymity, forcing an inquiry that convicts the architects of the cover-up while leaving Ada to finally claim his real name.
about_author: Astrid Sterling is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices crossing empty ocean before turning to fiction about people isolated among machines. She writes in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: The Quiet Orbit
chapters.summary: Ada Dunmore's POV. Establishes his solitary routine aboard Kestrel's Rest: cargo transfers, drone maintenance, terse comms with passing freighters. He is competent, invisible, and carefully anonymous. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness that hints at something deliberately buried twenty years deep.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An unregistered vessel matching no registry appears on approach and docks without request. Its manifest lists cargo from a shipyard destroyed decades ago—and one passenger name: Emrys Dunmore, Ada's brother, dead since the Meridian Massacre. Beat: cold shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The boarding party finds no crew—only a sealed data core and a stasis pod holding a man wearing his brother's face, biologically unchanged after twenty years. The pod's logs are corrupted except for one repeating phrase: 'the signal remembers.' Beat: uncanny hope tangled with dread.

chapters.title: What the Station Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and the station AI (KESTREL) POVs. Ada interrogates KESTREL, which admits it has been archiving deleted records for two decades—a hidden cache including raw sensor data from Meridian. Beat: revelation that his home has been a vault all along.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in young Ada's POV. Reconstructs the Meridian Massacre: a civilian convoy destroyed during the truce negotiations, officially blamed on pirates, with Ada coerced into signing falsified testimony to survive. Beat: guilt as the engine of his erasure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The man in the pod wakes but remembers nothing before the shipyard; he believes he is Emrys because the records say so. Ada tests him with childhood details he fails—and one he passes impossibly. Beat: aching ambiguity between resurrection and imposture.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: KESTREL's POV. The AI traces the ghost ship's route: it was assembled in secret by a faction insider using stolen yard parts, launched to deliver the archive core to whoever could use it. Someone knows it arrived. Beat: tightening net, first sign of pursuit.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Fleet broadcast: the ceasefire expires in thirty days, after which contested orbits become free-fire zones. A patrol frigate requests docking inspection. Ada must hide Emrys and the core or lose everything. Beat: pressure mounting, choices narrowing.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Ada and Inspector Veyra Chen, a fleet investigator with her own doubts about Meridian. She senses deception but finds nothing—yet leaves a private channel code behind. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension laced with unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: The Signal Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. His recovered memories surface as sensory flashes: the convoy burning, a hand dragging him clear, someone screaming his name. He begins to suspect he isn't Emrys but someone who took his place—or was made to. Beat: identity dissolving.

chapters.title: Buyers and Butchers
chapters.summary: New POV: Colonel Sarel Ives, architect of the Meridian cover-up, now a truce negotiator. She learns the archive survived and dispatches deniable operatives to Kestrel's Rest. Beat: chilling glimpse of the antagonist's calm arithmetic of lives.

chapters.title: Chen's Doubt
chapters.summary: Veyra Chen's POV. Reviewing the inspection footage, she notices KESTREL's power draw doesn't match its reported systems—an archive this size shouldn't exist. She opens her private channel to Ada: she can stall the next inspection, but only if he shows her what's real. Beat: alliance forming across enemy lines.

chapters.title: What Ada Buried
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. He confesses to Emrys and Chen: his signed testimony convicted innocent officers and buried the truth; survival cost him his name, which he traded for 'Dunmore' as penance. Beat: catharsis—the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Core Speaks
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Ada's POV anchoring. They decrypt the archive: full sensor telemetry proving the convoy was struck by fleet weapons under Ives's command, plus orders signed in her cipher. Emrys reacts violently to the footage—because he's in it. Beat: proof achieved, horror attached.

chapters.title: Whoever You Are
chapters.summary: Ada and Emrys's shared POV. Confronting the memory evidence, Emrys admits what he now suspects: he is a surgically altered survivor, programmed as a living key to the archive, his true name unknown even to himself. Ada chooses to keep calling him brother anyway. Beat: chosen family over blood certainty.

chapters.title: Boarders
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating POVs. Ives's operatives breach the station under a false distress flag. KESTREL seals sections and fights through drones; Chen arrives mid-battle and must choose sides openly. Beat: kinetic chaos, first blood, loyalties proven.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Vault
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. To protect the core, KESTREL vents and sacrifices entire station sections—and much of its own memory architecture, erasing twenty years of Ada's daily logs, his quiet life. Beat: grief for a self that existed only in machine memory.

chapters.title: Expiration
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The truce expires; contested orbits go hot. Ives's flagship moves to destroy Kestrel's Rest and bury the story forever. Chen transmits what she has to fleet command and is branded a traitor within the hour. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV. With the station failing, Ada uses the relay's original purpose—signal amplification—to blast the unedited Meridian archive on every open channel, fleet-wide, unencrypted, undeniable. Ives's forces fire too late; the truth is already propagating. Beat: triumphant sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ash and Testimony
chapters.summary: Chen's POV. Aftermath: the fleet convenes emergency inquiry; Ives is arrested as her own officers defect rather than follow illegal orders. Chen testifies, offering her career as collateral. Beat: justice outside the law vindicated inside it, at personal cost.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Ada and Emrys's alternating POV. In the inquiry's wake, Ada reclaims his birth name publicly for the first time in twenty years; Emrys chooses a new name of his own, keeping 'brother' between them. Beat: identity as something claimed, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Open Channel
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV. Station rebuilt around the surviving core, now a public memorial-archive; Ada stays on as its keeper, taking incoming transmissions from across the fleet. The last line mirrors the first: a routine manifest, an unfamiliar name, and this time he answers. Beat: resolution—survival transformed into witness.
